A smart pointer is a class that owns an object through a pointer and deletes it when ownership ends, so the pointer's own type states who owns the object instead of a comment.

The problem a raw pointer leaves open is who must delete the object it points to: a function that returns one, or a class that stores one, says nothing about that, so two owners that each believe they alone must delete it cause a double free, and no owner at all leaks it.
